blocks.title: What a ceramic coating does for your paint, and what it does not.
body: A ceramic coating is a liquid that is applied by hand to your paint, then hardens into a thin, glass-like layer that **bonds to the clear coat**. Once it cures, that layer is what takes the abuse instead of your paint.
Wax sits on top of the paint and washes off in weeks. A coating becomes part of the surface and **lasts for years**. Here is what you will actually notice:
checks: **Water and dirt slide off.** Rain beads up and runs, so the car stays cleaner between washes.
**Washing takes half the time.** Grime does not grip the surface, so a rinse and a gentle wash does the job.
**Michigan winters are less of a threat.** Road salt, brine and slush do not get to sit against bare clear coat.
**Bird droppings, bugs and tree sap** wipe off before they etch the paint.
**Deeper gloss.** Your paint looks wet and rich, and stays that way.
**What it will not do:** a coating is not armor. It will not stop rock chips or a key scratch, and it is not a substitute for washing.

blocks.title: Watch what water does.
blocks.intro: On bare paint, water spreads out and sits. On coated paint it pulls into tight beads and rolls away, which is why a coated car stays cleaner between washes.

blocks.title: Three ways to protect paint. One of them lasts.
blocks.intro: Wax and sealant both wear away and need reapplying. A ceramic coating bonds to the clear coat and becomes the surface everything touches.

blocks.title: Six steps from drop-off to a coated, cured, warrantied car.
blocks.intro: Most of the work happens before the coating touches your paint. Here is exactly what your vehicle goes through at our shop.

steps.title: Inspection and walk-through
steps.body: We look over your paint under shop lighting, note existing damage, and confirm the package and any add-ons with you before touching the car.

steps.title: Wash and decontamination
steps.body: Foam wash, then iron and tar removal and a clay treatment to pull out the embedded grit a normal wash leaves behind.

steps.title: Paint correction
steps.body: Swirls, light scratches and oxidation are machine polished out. This is the step that makes the coating look right, because a coating locks in whatever is underneath it.

steps.title: Panel wipe and prep
steps.body: Every panel is wiped down to strip polishing oils so the coating bonds directly to clean clear coat, not to residue.

steps.title: Coating application
steps.body: Applied by hand, panel by panel, by a certified technician in a controlled shop environment. Flashed and leveled so there are no high spots or streaking.

steps.title: Cure, inspect and hand-off
steps.body: The coating cures in the shop before pickup. You leave with a written warranty, an aftercare guide, and a free follow-up wash scheduled so the first maintenance wash is done right.

blocks.footnote: If you need to be somewhere while we work, Uber is covered for the drop-off and pickup. You can also ask about our [pick-up and drop-off valet service](/mobile-detailing/).

faq.q: How long does a ceramic coating actually last?
faq.a:
We offer 1, 3 and 5 year packages, and those numbers are what the coating is built to hold up to with normal use and proper washing. The bigger factors are how the vehicle is stored and how it is washed. A garaged car that gets hand washed will outlast one that lives outside and goes through a brush tunnel wash.

Every package comes with a written warranty and an aftercare guide so you know exactly how to keep it performing.

faq.q: How much does a ceramic coating cost?
faq.a:
It depends on your specific vehicle: its size, the current condition of the paint, and how much correction it needs before coating. A well kept sedan and a work truck with heavy swirls are very different jobs, so a price list would just be a guess.

Tell us what you drive and we will give you a real number, usually in the same conversation. [Request a free quote](#quote) or call [(586) 400-1303](tel:+15864001303).

faq.q: How long will my car be at your shop?
faq.a:
Plan on at least a full day, and longer when the paint needs more correction. The coating itself goes on relatively quickly. It is the decontamination, paint correction and cure time that take the hours, and rushing any of them shows in the finish.

We give you an exact window when we quote your vehicle. Uber is covered for drop-off and pickup, and we offer pick-up and drop-off valet service if you would rather not come to us at all.

faq.q: Is paint correction included, or is that extra?
faq.a:
Correction is included with every coating package. It is not an upsell. It is the step that makes the coating worth doing.

A coating is clear and it bonds to whatever is underneath. Apply it over swirls and scratches and you have sealed those in for years. We polish the defects out first, then coat. Heavily damaged paint may need a more involved multi-stage correction, which we flag during the quote rather than surprise you with later.

faq.q: Do I still have to wash my car?
faq.a:
Yes. A coating makes washing easier, not optional. Dirt and salt do not bond to the surface the way they do to bare clear coat, so a rinse and a gentle hand wash gets the car clean in about half the time.

What we do ask: skip the brush-style automatic washes. Those spinning brushes put swirls into any finish, coated or not. Touchless is fine.

faq.q: Will a coating stop rock chips and scratches?
faq.a:
No, and anyone telling you otherwise is overselling. A ceramic coating is a hard, thin chemical barrier. It resists chemical etching, UV fade, salt and light marring from washing. It is not physical impact protection.

If rock chips on the front end are your main concern, that is what [paint protection film](/paint-protection-film/) is for. Ask us and we will tell you honestly which one fits what you are worried about.

faq.q: Can you coat a brand new car? What about an older one?
faq.a:
Both, and new is the ideal time. The paint is in its best condition, so there is less correction needed and you are protecting it from day one. New cars still get decontaminated and prepped, because factory paint is rarely as clean as it looks.

Older vehicles absolutely can be coated. If the paint is faded or oxidized, correction does more work up front, but the result on a tired finish is often the more dramatic of the two.

faq.q: How soon after coating can I wash it or drive in the rain?
faq.a:
The coating cures in our shop before you pick the vehicle up, so normal driving is fine right away, rain included. There is a short window afterward where we ask you to hold off on washing while the coating fully hardens.

The exact timing is in the aftercare guide you get at pickup, and your free follow-up wash is scheduled so the first real wash is done correctly by us.

faq.q: Can you coat more than just the paint?
faq.a:
Yes. Windshield and exterior glass, wheels and trim can all be coated, and doing them in the same visit is far more efficient than coming back later.

Coated glass is the one most people underrate. Rain sheets off at highway speed and your wipers do noticeably less work through a Michigan winter.

Our shop is in Clinton Township and we serve Macomb and Oakland counties, including Sterling Heights, Shelby Township, Macomb Township, Rochester Hills, Troy and the surrounding communities. See [all service areas](/service-areas/).
